text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000129 bills 99215 far above what its patient complexity predicts, mostly on patients with few chronic conditions, yet the small documented sample supports every 99215 reviewed.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern leans toward upcoding: the 99215 share runs well above the all-provider rate in every complexity tier, and most 99215s fall on 0–1 condition patients, with sampled claims for minor or follow-up diagnoses such as rash (C0081138, C0081278), upper respiratory infection (C0081334) and aftercare (C0080993). Against that, all 10 documented 99215 claims were supported, including low-complexity C0080995 (osteoarthritis, high MDM at 45 minutes), so the records as written do not show unsupported billing. The documentation is thin, covering only about a sixth of the 99215s, and a note recording high MDM for a single stable condition could be accurate or could be templated to match the bill. The data-reviewed signal is weak, with only 2 notes lacking a lab or test line. A reviewer should first pull full charts for the low-complexity 99215s, especially symptom-only visits, and read the notes for cloned or boilerplate MDM language and for time statements that are not plausible for the visit."}
